questions.text:
A binary relation R on [latex]\mathbb{N}\times \mathbb{N}[/latex] is defined as follows: (a,b)R(c,d) if [latex]a \leq c[/latex] or [latex]b \leq d[/latex]. Consider the following propositions:
P: R is reflexive
Q: R is transitive
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Reflexive: (a, b) R (a, b) since [latex]a\le a[/latex] True
- Transitive fails: (3, 2) R (1, 3) because 2 [latex]\le[/latex] 3, and (1, 3) R (2, 1) because 1 [latex]\le[/latex] 2, but (3, 2) R (2, 1) needs 3 [latex]\le[/latex] 2 or 2 [latex]\le[/latex] 1 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] both false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both P and Q are true
P is true and Q is false.
P is false and Q is true
Both P and Q are false

questions.text: Which one of the following well-formed formulae in predicate calculus is NOT valid?
questions.solution:
Option 4 is not valid: take a domain {1, 2} with p(1), q(2) true and p(2), q(1) false. Then every x satisfies p(x) [latex]\vee[/latex] q(x), but neither "all p" nor "all q" holds.

Options 1-3 are standard valid implications.

Answer: Option 4

questions.text:
Consider a set U of 23 different compounds in a Chemistry lab. There is a subset S of U of 9 compounds, each of which reacts with exactly 3 compounds of U. Consider the following statements:

I. Each compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
II. At least one compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
III. Each compound in U n S reacts with an even number of compounds.

Which one of the above statements is ALWAYS TRUE?
questions.solution:
Model compounds as vertices and reactions as edges. The sum of all degrees is even (handshake lemma).

The 9 compounds in S have degree 3 each: total 27 (odd). So the degrees of U \ S must add to an odd number, which needs at least one odd degree there. Nothing forces every one to be odd.

Answer: Only II

questions.text: The value of the expression [latex]13^{99}[/latex](mod 17), in the range 0 to 16, is _________.
questions.solution:
[latex]13\equiv-4\pmod{17}[/latex], so [latex]13^2\equiv16\equiv-1[/latex] and [latex]13^4\equiv1[/latex].

[latex]99=4\times24+3\Rightarrow13^{99}\equiv13^3=13^2\cdot13\equiv-13\equiv4\pmod{17}[/latex]

Answer: 4

questions.text: Suppose the functions F and G can be computed in 5 and 3 nano seconds by functional units [latex]U_{F}[/latex] and [latex]U_{G}[/latex], respectively. Given two instances of [latex]U_{F}[/latex] and two instances of [latex]U_{G}[/latex], it is required to implement the computation [latex]F(G(X_{i}))[/latex] for [latex]1\leq i\leq 10[/latex]. Ignoring all other delays, the minimum time required to complete this computation is ________ nanoseconds.
questions.solution:
Each item needs G (3 ns) then F (5 ns). With 2 units of each, the F units are the bottleneck: 10 F computations on 2 units = 5 rounds [latex]\times[/latex] 5 ns = 25 ns.

F can start only after the first G results are ready (3 ns), and the G units keep feeding F in time after that.

Total = 3 + 25 = 28 ns

Answer: 28
